info.title: TabPFN Inference API
info.description:
TabPFN makes predictions on tabular data in a single request. Each request to
`POST /predict` fits on the training data in the body. Then it predicts the
test data in the same body.

## Sending a request

Send `application/json`. The predict route in the API reference has an example
body.

A table is row-oriented or column-oriented. A row-oriented table is a list of
rows. A column-oriented table is an object that maps each column name to its
values. `y_train` is a flat list with one target for each training row.

For large tables, send `multipart/form-data` with Parquet tables to `POST /predict_parquet`. `POST /predict` also accepts `multipart/form-data`, with CSV or Parquet tables.

- Send `x_train`, `y_train` and `x_test` as file parts. `X_train` and `X_test`
  are also accepted as part names. A file name is optional.
- Give a Parquet part the content type `application/vnd.apache.parquet`, and a
  CSV part `text/csv`. The content type decides how the container reads the
  part. `POST /predict_parquet` rejects a part that is not Parquet.
- A part without a content type, or with `application/octet-stream`, is read
  as Parquet if its content is Parquet. `POST /predict` reads it as CSV if
  it is not.
- Send the rest of the body as JSON in a `request` part. Send this part as a
  plain form field, not as a file. The container rejects a `request` file.

To compress a body, send it with `Content-Encoding: gzip`.

`task_config.task` is `classification` or `regression`. The task decides which
`predict_params` apply. You cannot set some `tabpfn_config` fields on this
container. The container rejects a request that sets one of these fields. It
does not ignore the field.

The deployment selects the model. The container rejects a request whose `model_version` names another model.

## Classification output types

| `output_type`      | `prediction`                                                | class labels in      |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| `probas` (default) | one row per test row, one column per class                  | `metadata.classes`   |
| `preds`            | one label per test row                                      | `metadata.classes`   |
| `top_k`            | `{"classes": […], "values": [[…]], "probabilities": [[…]]}` | `prediction.classes` |

The classes are in ascending order and keep their original type.

With `top_k`, `values[j][i]` is a position in `prediction.classes`. To get the
class, use `classes[values[j][i]]`. Each row lists the classes from the most
probable to the least probable. If `top_k` is larger than the number of
classes, each row lists all classes. The probabilities in a row add up to 1
only when the row lists all classes. `top_k` is required with this output
type. The container rejects `top_k` with other output types.

## Regression output types

`mean` (default), `median`, `mode`, `quantiles`, `main` (the point estimates and
the quantiles), and `full`. Set `quantiles: [...]` to select the quantiles. If
you do not set `quantiles`, the container uses the default list. `full` returns
the full predicted distribution, so it accepts fewer rows.

## Usage counts

Each successful response has a `usage` block. The counts are for the tables as
you sent them, before preprocessing. You can calculate each count from the
request body. For a multipart body, the counts are for the files as the
container reads them. A CSV header row is not a row.

- `num_cells` is the total number of cells in the three tables.
- `num_predictions` is one for each test row. The `output_type` does not change
  this number.
- `n_estimators` is the ensemble size that the request used.

Use `usage` for metering. Do not use `metadata` for metering. Its widths
describe the table after preprocessing, which can remove or expand columns.

## Size limits

The container rejects a request over one of these limits with `422`.
Preprocessing can add columns, for example for text columns. The column and
cell limits also apply to the table that preprocessing makes.

| Limit                           | `v4`           |
| ------------------------------- | -------------- |
| Training rows                   | 10,000,000     |
| Columns                         | 20,000         |
| Training cells (rows × columns) | 20,480,000,000 |
| Test rows                       | 1,000,000      |
| Test cells                      | 2,048,000,000  |

Each table can take at most 10 GiB in memory after the container reads
it.

## Data in your object store

The operator can let the container read tables from your object store. A JSON
request can then give a table as `{"url": "..."}`, not as values. The URL is a
presigned GET URL of a Parquet or CSV object:

```json
{
  "task_config": { "task": "classification", "tabpfn_config": {} },
  "X_train": { "url": "https://store.example/bucket/x_train.parquet?X-Amz-Signature=..." },
  "y_train": { "url": "https://store.example/bucket/y_train.parquet?X-Amz-Signature=..." },
  "X_test": { "url": "https://store.example/bucket/x_test.parquet?X-Amz-Signature=..." }
}
```

The container has no credentials for the store. It reads only URLs on the hosts
that the operator allows, and it does not follow a redirect. It does not write
a URL to its log or to a response.

If the store refuses a URL (expired, forbidden or missing), the container
returns `422`. If the store fails (`5xx`, throttling or no answer), the
container returns `503`. Send the request again.

You can send `X_test` as values with training data by URL. Then `X_test` must
use the column names of the stored tables (`{"f0": [...], "f1": [...]}`). A
list of rows gives the columns by position only.

## Request ids and errors

Each response has an `X-Request-Id` header, and each error body has a
`trace_id`. Both give the id of the request in the container's log. Give this
id when you report a problem.

To use your own id, send it in a header. The container uses the first of these
headers that it finds: `Sentry-Trace`, `X-Cloud-Trace-Context`, `traceparent`,
`X-Request-Id`, `b3` or `X-B3-TraceId`, and `X-Amzn-Trace-Id`. A trace id is
32 or 16 hex digits, or a UUID.

An `X-Request-Id` that is not a trace id is returned unchanged, and the log
shows it next to an id that the container makes. This applies only to a value
of 128 printable characters or fewer, with no spaces. The container ignores a
different value.

An error body always has these three fields:

```json
{
  "message": "Invalid request. categorical_features_indices [99] do not name a column: the data has 4 columns, indexed from 0.",
  "error_code": "USER_ERROR",
  "trace_id": "0af7651916cd43dd8448eb211c80319c"
}
```

Use `error_code` in your code. `message` tells what is wrong with this request
and what to do, and its text can change between releases. A `400`, `415` or
`422` status with `USER_ERROR` always means that you must change the request
before it can succeed.

| `error_code`               | Status | Cause                                                                   | What to do                                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `USER_ERROR`               | 400    | The request is malformed or names a value the endpoint does not accept. | Correct the field the message names and resend.                                            |
| `REQUEST_VALIDATION_ERROR` | 422    | A field has the wrong type or shape.                                    | Correct the field the message names and resend.                                            |
| `NOT_FOUND`                | 404    | The path does not exist on this deployment.                             | Use the predict path given in the release notes.                                           |
| `CACHE_NOT_ENABLED`        | 400    | This deployment does not keep fitted models between requests.           | Send the training data with every request and do not set `fit_mode` or `context.model_id`. |
| `OUT_OF_MEMORY`            | 413    | The request did not fit in the memory of the device it ran on.          | Retry once; if it repeats, send fewer rows or columns, or lower `n_estimators`.            |
| `BUSY`                     | 503    | The deployment is at capacity.                                          | Retry after the interval in the `Retry-After` header.                                      |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR`           | 500    | The container failed while serving the request.                         | Report the `trace_id` to your provider.                                                    |

A `413` with `USER_ERROR` means that the body is larger than the free memory of
the container. Send fewer rows, or deploy on an instance with more memory.

post.summary: Fit on the training data and predict the test data

400.description:
The container cannot use the body:

* The container cannot parse the body.
* The body has no `task_config` or no `X_test`.
* A `task_config` value is not valid.
* The body is compressed but is not valid gzip.
* `fit_mode` is `fit_with_cache`. This container does not keep fits.

413.description: The body, after decompression, is larger than the container accepts.

415.description: The body is not JSON or multipart form data, its `Content-Encoding` is not `gzip`, or a file part is not CSV or Parquet.

422.description:
The request is not valid:

* A field has a value that is not valid.
* `X_train` or `y_train` is missing.
* The request sets a field that you cannot set on this container.
* The data or the requested output is larger than the container accepts.
* `model_version` names a model other than the one the deployment selects.

500.description: The prediction failed in the container.

503.description:
The container cannot serve the request now. Retry the request later.

* The container is at its request limit.
* No device became free in time.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying, when supplied.

request.description: The rest of the body, as JSON. Send it as a plain form field, not as a file.

x_train.description: Training features, as CSV with a header row or as Parquet.

y_train.description: Training targets, as CSV or Parquet with one column. A CSV file has a header row.

x_test.description: Features to predict, as CSV with a header row or as Parquet.

request.description: The rest of the body, as JSON. Send it as a plain form field, not as a file.

y_train.description: Training targets, as Parquet with one column.

test_set_num_rows.description: Number of rows that the model predicted.

test_set_num_cols.description: Number of columns after encoding. This number can be different from the number of columns that you sent.

n_estimators.description: Ensemble size that the request used. Null when no ensemble ran.

package_version.description: Version of the TabPFN package that made the prediction.

tabpfn_config.description: The model settings that the request used.

classes.description: Class labels in ascending order. They name the columns of `probas` and the labels of `preds`. Null with `top_k`, because `top_k` has its own `prediction.classes`.

n_estimators.description: Ensemble size. The model averages this number of forward passes, and each pass uses a different preprocessed view of the data. If unset, TabPFN selects the size. It selects 8 for most data. For wide tables, it selects more, so that each column gets to at least one ensemble member.

categorical_features_indices.description: 0-based indices of the categorical columns. If unset, the model finds the categorical columns.

softmax_temperature.description: A lower value makes the predicted probabilities more confident. The value 1.0 has no effect. If unset, the model uses its default value.

average_before_softmax.description: If true, the model averages the logits of the ensemble members before the softmax. If false, it averages their probabilities after the softmax. `auto` takes the setting of the checkpoint, as does unset. A true or false value cannot be combined with `AVERAGE_BEFORE_SOFTMAX` in `inference_config`.

random_state.description: Random seed. The same seed gives the same results. If unset, TabPFN uses its default seed.

inference_config.description: Advanced inference settings. See `tabpfn.inference_config.InferenceConfig` in the TabPFN package.

inference_precision.description: `autocast` always uses mixed precision. `auto` selects the precision from the hardware.

presets.description: Names of bundles of inference settings. `zero_inflated` is for regression targets with many exact zeros. The keys of `inference_config` win over every preset. If unset, the model uses the settings of its checkpoint.

n_preprocessing_jobs.description: Number of worker processes for preprocessing.

fit_mode.description: How the model prepares the fit.

memory_saving_mode.description: If true, the model divides parts of the computation into batches to use less memory. If unset, the model decides.

balance_probabilities.description: If true, the model adjusts the probabilities for the class distribution of the training data. This can help with imbalanced classes when the metric ignores class imbalance, such as balanced accuracy.

X_train.description: Shape of `X_train` as you sent it. Zero when the request has no training data.

y_train.description: Shape of `y_train` as you sent it. Zero when the request has no training data.

X_test.description: Shape of `X_test` as you sent it.

n_estimators.description: Ensemble size that the request used. Never null.

num_cells.description: Total number of cells in the three tables.

num_predictions.description: One for each test row. The `output_type` does not change this number.

InputUsage.description:
What the request used. Use it for metering.

The counts are for the tables as you sent them, before preprocessing. You can
calculate each count from the request body. `metadata.test_set_num_cols` is
different: it is the width after encoding.

TableUsage.description: Shape of one input table, as you sent it.

output_type.description:
What `prediction` contains:

* `probas`: one probability for each class, for each row.
* `preds`: one label for each row.
* `top_k`: the most probable classes for each row.

top_k.description: Number of classes that `top_k` returns for each row. Required with `output_type=top_k`. Other output types do not permit it.

output_type.description:
What `prediction` contains:

* `mean`, `median` or `mode`: one value for each row.
* `quantiles`: one list for each quantile.
* `main`: the mean, median, mode and quantiles.
* `full`: the full predicted distribution. It accepts fewer rows.

quantiles.description: Quantile levels between 0 and 1, for `quantiles` and `main`. If unset, TabPFN uses its default list of 9 levels.

PredictRequest.description: Training and test data, and how to predict.

task_config.description: The task, model settings and output type.

tabpfn_systems.description:
The preparation steps that run on the tables before the model. With `[]`, the model gets the tables with only minimal cleaning.

* `preprocessing` cleans and encodes the columns. On v4 it adds no character n-gram features and keeps every feature it generates.
* `text` embeds the text columns, as part of `preprocessing`.

oneOf.description: Row-oriented: one inner list per row.
Column-oriented: column name to its values.
By URL, on a deployment that allows the URL's host.

label_reliability.description: How far to trust each target of `y_train`, one value in [0, 1] per row. Needs a model that takes weights, and a fit that the container does not keep.

PredictRequestPart.description: The fields of the JSON body, without `X_train`, `y_train` and `X_test`. Send the tables as file parts.
